definitions.explanation: The act of bringing a chaotic or problematic situation under control. Often used when a situation has spiraled out of hand and needs to be contained or resolved.

examples.japanese: {事態|じたい}の{収拾|しゅうしゅう}に{当|あ}たる。
examples.english: To work on bringing the situation under control.

examples.japanese: {混乱|こんらん}が{広|ひろ}がり、{収拾|しゅうしゅう}がつかなくなった。
examples.english: The chaos spread and became impossible to control.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}が{自|みずか}ら{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}を{開|ひら}いて{事態|じたい}の{収拾|しゅうしゅう}を{図|はか}った。
examples.english: The president personally held a press conference to try to bring the situation under control.

notes:
USAGE:
Often appears in news and formal contexts describing crisis management. The most common pattern is {収拾|しゅうしゅう}がつかない (to be out of control, beyond settling).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {収拾|しゅうしゅう}がつかない (to be out of control)
- {収拾|しゅうしゅう}を{図|はか}る (to attempt to bring under control)
- {収拾|しゅうしゅう}に{当|あ}たる (to handle the resolution)
- {事態|じたい}の{収拾|しゅうしゅう} (resolution of the situation)

WATCH OUT:
- {収集|しゅうしゅう}: collection, gathering — same reading, but means to collect items (e.g., ゴミ{収集|しゅうしゅう} "garbage collection")
- {収拾|しゅうしゅう} uses {拾|しゅう} (pick up), not {集|しゅう} (gather)
